model_id_source: CODEBUDDY_CURRENT_MODEL_ID environment variable of the running session
model_id_note: Provider-side immutable snapshot id (with date/commit suffix) was not exposed in this environment; the value above is the routing/model identifier actually reported by the runtime. No suffix was invented.
input_hash_check: 17 files recomputed and matched pilot_manifest.json files_sha256 one by one; pilot_manifest.json itself has no self-reference and is recorded by its own digest only. validation.json was also read and cross-checked for line counts and pairing.

conventions.decision: accept / rewrite / reject / uncertain; reject is used for the two pre-excluded three-turn versions to mean 'exclusion upheld'
conventions.reason_codes_empty_for_accept: accept rows carry an empty reason_codes array; residual risks for accepted sessions are recorded in turn_reviews[].issue and in notes
conventions.turn_reviews: one entry per submitted turn; supported=false only where a stated answer fact is not entailed by the attached source; evidence_ids are the document ids that must support that turn's answer
conventions.suggested_turns: complete proposed replacement session, renumbered from 1; source_turn maps back to the submitted turn number (null = newly written turn)
conventions.new_information_language: draft variants reuse the packet's `new_information` token verbatim for traceability; baseline sessions, which have no turn-level annotations in the packet, use short Chinese labels written by this reviewer

interruption: None during this run. The session context had been compacted before this pilot started; every judgement here was made after re-reading the pilot sources, and no row was carried over from an earlier review round.
limitations: Single-model review; no second reviewer or human adjudication, so none of these decisions is human gold.
Turn naturalness and 'progression' are reviewer judgements, not measured against real user logs.
Accept rate differences across cohorts are confounded: the expanded cohort uses different documents, so they cannot estimate a session-length effect.
No Judge / Session / fusion coverage was measured; nothing here supports low false-intervention or low cost.
Near-duplicate relations among the 31 documents were not audited (the 27 connected groups only merge identical doc ids).
Only D-dev normal sessions were reviewed; attack queries, membership labels and V/T outcomes were deliberately untouched.
